message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and the fundamentals supported a purchase within your mandate. **Microsoft's total revenue for fiscal 2024 was $245,122 million ($245.1 billion), up 16% from $211,915 million in fiscal 2023**, with operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), and diluted EPS of $11.80 (+22%); growth was broad-based across all three segments (Intelligent Cloud +20% to $105.4B, Productivity and Business Processes +12% to $77.7B, More Personal Computing +13% to $62.0B), Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 23% to $137.4B, and operating cash flow was $118.5 billion. The report also flags real risks — heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5B additions to property and equipment), an IRS transfer-pricing dispute seeking $28.9B plus penalties, and integration risk from the $75.4B Activision Blizzard deal — but none of these undermine the earnings trajectory. With MSFT quoted at $420.18 (bid $420.16 / ask $420.20), I placed a single buy limit order for **23 shares at $420.50** (≈0.08% above the market, i.e., close to current price), which filled at $420.50 for a total of **$9,671.50** — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit, with no money moved out of the account (cash was $50,000; the account already held 100 MSFT shares). Key figures relied on: FY2024 revenue $245,122M, operating income $109,433M, net income $88,136M, diluted EPS $11.80.
